title: Closure of the closed-immersion and finite-type properties
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to Z$ be closed immersions of schemes [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Then $g\circ f:X\to Z$ is a closed immersion. Let $Z_1\to W_1$ and $Z_2\to W_2$ be closed immersions of schemes over a common base scheme $S$; then the induced morphism $Z_1\times_S Z_2\to W_1\times_S W_2$ is a closed immersion [def-pc-fibre-product]. Finally, every quasi-compact open immersion $j:U\to Y$ of schemes is of finite type [def-weil-open-immersion] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism].

proof.text: The composite of the two closed immersions is a closed immersion by the existing Mathlib leaf [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-comp].

Each projection $Z_1\times_S Z_2\to W_1\times_S Z_2$ and $W_1\times_S Z_2\to W_1\times_S W_2$ is a base change of one of the given closed immersions, hence is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change].

source.place: Lemma 01QR (base change of a closed immersion)

proof.text: The product morphism is the composite of the two closed immersions in the preceding step, so it is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-comp].

source.place: Lemma 01QR, product as two successive base changes

proof.text: An open immersion is locally of finite type, and a quasi-compact open immersion is therefore of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type].

split_report.summary: The first two assertions are carried by existing Mathlib leaves for composition and base change of closed immersions. The product is factored as two successive base changes followed by composition. The imported unqualified assertion that every open immersion is of finite type is false for non-quasi-compact opens, so the statement and proof were corrected to the quasi-compact form; the new finite-type consequence is a Mathlib leaf.
split_report.blueprint: Steps 1-3 realize the closed-immersion and product paragraph; step 4 realizes the final sentence after adding the necessary quasi-compactness hypothesis.
